title: Leaving Cab: Greely Walton replaces him and he joins Don Redman
summary: Having a job lined up, Thomas gives notice, Cab insists he find a replacement, and he finds Greely Walton before going with Redman.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Quitting the band: why sidemen left

blocks.x: This is way ahead of myself. But I got ready to leave. We was playing the Sheraton. I had made a deal to go... I'd already got me a gig. Because Jefferson always told me, he said, "Man, if you want a raise, always have somewhere to go if you can't get it and you're going to get fired."

So I had already gone and got me a job. I went by... I didn't know Don [Redman] that well, but Don knew me. So I went by and told him I was thinking about leaving the band. He said, "Man, you got a job. Whenever you leave, you've got a job." Because he needed a saxophone

player. So I told him about when I was leaving... So you know, you had to give your notice on payday, or the first day after payday. So payday I told Fess, I said, "Fess, I've got to give you my notice." "You can't give me your notice!" I said, "Why?" "You've got to get somebody to take your place!" Well, see, I was involved in getting musicians and all of that. But that's just what he said! So I had to go out and find me a saxophone player that played flute and clarinet and piano -- and I found Greely. And that's how I got out of the band. Because otherwise... And I had done told my wife I was...
Yeah, I remember Greely coming in the band, but I didn't remember the year...

Because see, he didn't have to play no solos or nothin'. All he had to do was come in and play the parts. And I knew him, so I got Greely. And that's how I got out of the band. And then I went right straight to Don
Redman. That was a great experience.
